new_sources.author: Janet Griffitts
new_sources.title: Faunal analysis of two charcoal samples from the cave beneath the Sun Pyramid

findings.subject: Griffitts 2007 faunal specimen distribution
findings.assertion: The 2007 laboratory report recorded 978 faunal fragments in two analyzed samples: 969 in TE28:C fire pit and 9 in TE28:B SF15. At least 513 shell fragments were recorded, of which 504 were shorter than 5 mm; columella fragments suggested 3 to 5 individual snails. These numbers describe the analyzed samples only.
findings.locator: Griffitts 2007, PDF printed pp.1,3-4, Tables 2-3; original PDF page screenshots examined
findings.limitations: Highly fragmented assemblage; 513+ shell count is minimum; not representative of all deposits; MNI is inferred.

findings.subject: Snail genus ambiguity and unavailable fishbone
findings.assertion: Griffitts reports that shell fragments could be Sonorella (terrestrial) or Helisoma (freshwater), which cannot be securely distinguished; fish bone recorded by excavators was no longer available for the 2007 examination. Human transport in fish or attached vegetation and rodent transport remain hypothetical pathways.
findings.locator: Griffitts 2007, PDF pp.1-2, Shell and Fishbone; Cultural Significance and Taphonomy, original screenshots examined
findings.limitations: Taxa are ambiguous; missing fishbone prevents independent check; no proof of offerings or freshwater origin.

findings.subject: Blackened rodent fragments and taphonomy
findings.assertion: The faunal analyst identified only three blackened rodent-sized fragments, which might reflect heat or mineral staining. She observed no other clear burning or cultural modifications in the analyzed bone and shell and judged identified rodents likely intrusive.
findings.locator: Griffitts 2007, PDF p.2 and p.4 Table 3, original screenshots examined
findings.limitations: Report covers a restricted faunal subset; cannot establish absence of ancient ritual in the entire cave; cause of blackening indeterminate.

findings.subject: Heyden July 1974 cave-origin and water hypothesis
findings.assertion: In a letter to Jorge Acosta dated 29 July 1974, Doris Heyden stated that the cave appeared after ground subsidence during heavy rains in autumn 1971, interpreted it as a natural grotto, and proposed an ancient stream and sanctuary based partly on stone drain tubes and covers. This documents her 1974 interpretation, not established cave geology or ritual history.
findings.locator: Heyden to Jorge Acosta, 29 July 1974, scanned letter pp.1-2; numbered statements 1-3, original pages visually examined
findings.limitations: Later excavators argue the tunnel was artificial; original Acosta field records were not consulted.
